packet-01 - first reader response (unverified image reading)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. Blind reading.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1; packet has four overviews: 001, 011, 021, 031, each followed by nine native tiles in a 3x3 grid)

image-001: two separate paper pieces photographed together, one above the other, with ruler (top) and colour checker (bottom right). Both are bifolium-width sheets with a central vertical fold.
- Upper piece (pencil/ink shelfmark lower right reads "Stams, StA, Frg. 27-1a" or similar): German text in a large, rather unpractised cursive (Kurrent), written across each half of the fold separately (left half c. 11 lines, right half c. 12 lines), i.e. the same or a similar text repeated on left and right halves. Below the text on each half: a ruled line, then two lines of alphabet letters written out (an ABC / letter row), then a ruled line, then a name/signature line ("Christianus ..." on both halves; left one followed by further words and a second line with numerals/date?). Appearance: a writing exercise (Schreibvorlage / pupil copy). Large flourished capital letters (repeated pen trials, looks like "F"/"S"/"L" forms) drawn in the central gutter area of the right half.
- Lower piece (shelfmark at top right "Stams, StA, Frg. 27-2a"?): text in a larger Fraktur/Kanzlei-like formal hand, again on two halves. Left half begins with an enlarged initial (W?) "Weillen ..."; right half also begins "Weillen ..." with flourished W. Repeated large flourished capitals in the gutter (pen trials). Left half shows remnant words of another column at the far left edge (cut). Below the formal lines the left half has fainter cursive lines (lower part, partly very faded). Right half has two alphabet rows, then cursive lines, then a separate block in a Latin textura/Fraktur-like hand beginning "Magnificat anima mea ..." (looks like a Latin script exercise).
- Tentative interpretation: school/writing exercise sheets (model text copied twice, alphabet rows, signature of the pupil). Not a book manuscript.


=== FACE 1 (image-001), upper piece, left half ===
image-002 (top-left tile; left edge of sheet, text cut at right edge of tile)
Hand: large unpractised German Kurrent, c. 12 text lines, then ruled line, then alphabet row. Brown stain, ink faint in places.
002/01  [top line cut at sheet edge; only descenders visible] [illegible]
002/02  [..]eben? liebar? komme(n) die vorig[...]
002/03  [..]wegiß? mit ? ? vnd [...]   (hole after "mit"; very uncertain)
002/04  vor der nöd? meine(n)? mund so w[...]
002/05  [e]rhöchten? vnd zu verpf? ehen?[...]
002/06  kind zu Gott vnd vnser[...]
002/07  [..]ch durch dein hoffnung vnd v[...]
002/08  Maria? ... für vns dainy? li[...]   ("Maria" uncertain; tall long-s/f in middle)
002/09  vnd Gott damit mein huld[...]
002/10  vnd sonderlichen vnsere(n) Ab[...]
002/11  [V?]keinen? sünden ... hör? die wor[t...]
002/12  [..]...kart? auf daß ihr die rechten? [...]
002/13  [ruled line]
002/14  [alphabet row] r? a b c d e f g h i [k...]
002/15  [second alphabet row, cut at bottom]
Note: lines 002/02-12 correspond to the same lines seen in overview right half (text repeated), compare with tiles of the right half.

image-003 (top-middle tile: line-ends of left half, central fold with pen-trial loops/flourished capitals (F/T forms), and line-starts of right half). Overlaps image-002 by roughly the "...vorig", "...vnd", "...so w" region.
Left half, line ends (numbered to match 002 lines):
003/02 = 002/02  ...die vorig?h?it? m? vmbar?   (one long word, cannot resolve)
003/03 = 002/03  ...[mu]ndt? vnd vergehet? / verzicht?
003/04 = 002/04  ...[mun]de so wirdt für dich
003/05 = 002/05  ...[...]ehen? bringen Mein
003/06 = 002/06  ...vnd vnser lieben frauen
003/07 = 002/07  ...vnd vertrauen d[...]   ("vertrauen" fairly clear; final letter d? at line end)
003/08 = 002/08  ...dainy? lieben sohn.
003/09 = 002/09  ...[mein] huld erwerben
003/10 = 002/10  ...vnsere(n) Ab?sterbe(n)? ama?,   (last word looks like "ama," or "Amen,")
003/11 = 002/11  ...[d]ie wort fünd? / sünd?
003/12 = 002/12  ...rechten verstandt
003/13 [ruled line]
003/14 [alphabet row, cont.] ... h i k l m n o p q? r? s? t? y? z?   (letters spaced; reading of last letters uncertain)
So left-half connected reading (002+003), tentative:
  ... kommen die vorig?...
  ... vor der nöd? meine(n) mund so wirdt für dich
  erhöchten? vnd zu verpf?..ehen bringen Mein
  kind zu Gott vnd vnser lieben frauen
  ..ch durch dein hoffnung vnd vertrauen d..
  Maria? ... für vns dainy? lieben sohn.
  vnd Gott damit mein huld erwerben
  vnd sonderlichen vnsere(n) Ab..sterbe? ama?,
  ...keinen sünden hör? die wort fünd?
  ...kart? auf daß ihr die rechten verstandt
Right half, line starts visible at right edge of tile: wor[t], wer?[...], vnd?[...], mi[t?], für, brin[gen], vnser, hoffn[ung], aller?, lieb[en], erwo[rben], Ama[n?]
Gutter: large looped pen trials (an elaborate capital with ovals near top; flourished capital T/F at mid-lower) - not text.

=== FACE 1, upper piece, right half ===
image-004 (top-right tile; right half of upper piece, right sheet edge visible). Same hand (or a very similar one), same text as left half but with different line breaks - a second copy.
004/01  [top line cut; tops of letters only] [illegible]
004/02  wort aufnemen vnd halt[en]
004/03  wenigsten? über? überkhommen, [...]   ("überkhomen" fairly clear; first word uncertain)
004/04  minder? [..]wegiß? mit ker? s[...]   (hole in the paper between "minder" and "-wegiß")
004/05  mit kor? der nöd meines? m[und?]
004/06  für dich erhöchen vnd zu [...]
004/07  bringen Mein kind zu G[ott]
004/08  vnser lieben frauen pz? [...]
004/09  hoffnung vnd vertrauen d[...]
004/10  aller vnser noth bitt für [vns?]
004/11  lieben sohn vnd Gott dam[it]
004/12  erwerben vnd sonderlichen v[nsere(n)?]
004/13  Amen   (written "Aman"/"Amen" with flourish)
004/14  [ruled line]; below it the start of an alphabet row (cut).
Collation note (my inference from the two copies, not a supplied reading): left 002/08 "...für vns dainy? lieben sohn" parallels right "bitt für [vns] ... lieben sohn"; left 003/10 "...ama," = right 004/13 "Amen". So the end of the text is "...vnd sonderlichen vnsere(n) Ab..(?) Amen". The right half lacks the two final lines of the left half (002/11-12 "...die wort fünd? / ...auf daß ihr die rechten verstandt") before "Amen"? - unclear; possibly those belong to a different sentence on the left half. Left half 002/11-12 may continue after "Amen," (i.e. a following sentence: "...hör? die wort ... auf daß ihr die rechten verstandt").

image-005 (middle-left tile). Top part = bottom of upper piece, left half; lower part = top of lower piece, left half. Overlaps image-002 at its last lines (002/11-15).
Upper piece, left half (continuing 002):
005/01 = 002/11  [V?]keinen? sünden hör? die wor[t...]

005/03  [ruled line]
